additionalReviewedPreparations.status: Research-only targeted historical near-infrared map-methods review
findings: Sections5.1.2–5.1.5 select an inner disk ROI because limb projection and deconvolution ringing degrade pixels; per-night selection is not independently reproduced.

The planetocentric system uses0–360degrees right-hand longitude relative to spin, prime meridian along positive-x long axis and positive latitude toward spin. This historical convention is not automatically the2020ESO display or any adopted texture frame.
Northern and southern data did not overlap. Authors set their relative brightness by assuming equal mean hemispheric albedo, not by a measured cross-hemisphere photometric tie.

J/H/K composite maps combine27/44/115 individual projections respectively, not necessarily that many independent raw exposures. Publisher reports80percent K versus40percent J/H coverage and approximately60km resolution; these are cited estimates, not new raster calculations.

Reported within-band±6percent variations, approximately4percent maximal and below2.5percent mean dispersion are internal source-product estimates, not independently verified absolute visible photometry.

Authors explicitly allow the northern modeled depression to be an inversion artefact because the shape fit omitted albedo information. Possible crater interpretation is not uniquely established geography.

Weak spectral-region differences can reflect morphology, composition or grain properties. These do not quantify mapped local chemistry. Io/Titan/Ceres/Vesta comparisons are methodological context, never substitute skins.

findings: Fig7 separates north/south K-band albedo panels on left from error panels on right, with an equatorial cylindrical albedo map between. Error imagery must not be assigned as terrain/albedo.

White regions explicitly mark terra incognita from limited ROI and observation orientation, including much of equatorial region. White is not measured ice, smooth terrain, a crater or complete mapped coverage.
Albedo legend is percent relative to mean, approximately-7to+7; error legend0to4percent. Neither is absolute geometric albedo, visible RGB, elevation or local material fraction.
The common albedo gray scale across three views does not remove the separate methodological assumption of equal north/south mean brightness from Section5.1.5.

Caption reports approximately80percent coverage, approximately±6percent albedo variations and4percent maximum error. Southern mapping is coarser due fewer images; these remain publisher estimates, not newly computed raster scales/independent calibration.
Caption confidence that features have very low artefact probability is an author claim, not independently reproduced validation; Section5.2 still discusses deconvolution and shape/albedo ambiguity.

Publisher reports 27 J and44 H projections versus115 K, coarser J/H maps, variations within approximately6percent of each map mean and estimated maximum4percent errors. These are reported relative-map estimates, not independently reproduced absolute photometry or new raster computations.

findings: Table5 explicitly reports triaxial RADII and volume-equivalent mean radius, not full diameters: this work275/258/238km, mean256km; Drummond274/252/230 mean251; Schmidt291/278/250 mean272. These historical alternatives are not replacements for current Marsset/JPL values.
Table5 dimension errors derive from the population standard deviation of per-image scale factors fitted to asteroid contours, not independent proof of surface accuracy or all systematic errors.

Fig5 compares model outlines with four occultations1978May29/1983May29/1985Oct24/2001Jun9. Diamonds are disappearance/reappearance times, dashed lines chords and solid segments observer-stated timing errors; celestial north up/east left. No chords were newly digitized or converted.

The1983 southeast facet has approximately20km mismatch reported by authors. Albedo omitted during inversion may mimic a depression; neither the facet nor a crater is independently confirmed local terrain.

Fig6 gray bars are chord endpoints/errors and black bands model contours with uncertainty; radial plane-of-sky azimuth is counterclockwise from celestial north through east, not a body-fixed longitude map.

Table6 expressly says residuals are NOT goodness of fit because the model was not adjusted to those values. The1978 KAO-inclusive row7chords/RMS12.9km/6.1sigma differs from six-chord row6.2km/1.3sigma, with figure-centre readjusted; deleting a chord is not an authorized correction to raw observations.

Historical density3.4±.9g/cm3 adopts Michalak2000 mass and is mass-uncertainty dominated. Drier-than-Ceres interpretation, hydration/interior/porosity alternatives and historical spectral nondetections do not establish present local chemistry, water absence or calibrated geography.
